quizzes.question: In Nepal, this mountain is known locally as Sagarmatha, meaning 'Forehead of the Sky,' while in Tibet it is called Chomolungma. Formed by the ongoing tectonic collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates, its region above 8,000 meters is famously designated as the 'Death Zone.' First officially summited in 1953 by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, it stands as the highest mountain on Earth. For the point, name this peak in the Himalayas.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest, known as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet, is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Himalayas.

quizzes.question: Centripetal forms of this vector quantity direct an object toward the center of a circular path and are calculated as velocity squared divided by radius. According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, this property is directly proportional to the net force applied to an object and inversely proportional to its mass. Near Earth's surface, its standard value due to gravity is approximately 9.81 meters per second squared. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of an object's velocity over time, measured in meters per second squared (m/s²).

quizzes.question: In 1865, the Royal Geographical Society officially named this peak after British surveyor-general Sir George Everest following a recommendation by Andrew Waugh. Situated in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range, it straddles the international border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. Rising to an officially recognized elevation of 8,848.86 meters, it is celebrated as the highest point on Earth. For the point, name this Himalayan mountain.
quizzes.explanation: Named after Sir George Everest in 1865, Mount Everest reaches an elevation of 8,848.86 meters on the Nepal-Tibet border.

quizzes.question: Einstein's Equivalence Principle states that standing on a massive body experiencing this fundamental interaction is indistinguishable from being in a uniformly accelerating frame of reference. Newton described this interaction using an inverse-square law involving a constant approximately equal to 6.674 times 10 to the negative 11th power. Although it is the weakest of the four fundamental forces, it dominates at astronomical scales because it is strictly attractive and operates over infinite distances. For the point, name this force that pulls objects toward Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is an attractive fundamental interaction calculated classically by Newton's law of universal gravitation and explained modernly by General Relativity.

quizzes.question: Mountaineers attempting to reach this peak must navigate extreme risks in the 'Death Zone,' where atmospheric pressure drops significantly and oxygen levels are dangerously low. The Tibetan name for this peak translates to 'Mother Goddess of the World,' honoring its spiritual significance along the Himalayan range. Climbed successfully for the first time in May 1953 by Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary, it is the tallest of the Seven Summits. For the point, name this highest mountain above sea level.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest's high altitude zone is known as the Death Zone, and its Tibetan name is Chomolungma ('Mother Goddess of the World').

quizzes.question: In calculus, taking the second derivative of position with respect to time yields this physical vector quantity. It is measured in SI units of meters per second squared and occurs whenever an object changes its speed, direction of motion, or both. In the equation F = ma derived from Newton's second law, this quantity is represented by the variable lower-case a. For the point, name this physical quantity representing how rapidly velocity changes.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is represented by 'a' in Newton's formula F = ma and measures the rate of change of velocity.

quizzes.question: The tectonic collision that built this landmark involves the Indian Plate actively pushing against and subducting under the Eurasian Plate. Surveyors Andrew Waugh and Sir George Everest played key roles in establishing its position and height during the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India. Located in the Mahalangur Himal range on the border between Nepal and China, it reaches 29,031.7 feet in height. For the point, name this world-famous mountain peak.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest was measured during the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India and was formed via the tectonic collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates.

quizzes.question: Modern physics describes this phenomenon not as a direct mechanical pull, but as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. It acts across infinite distances, is strictly attractive, and causes free-falling objects near Earth to accelerate at 9.81 meters per second squared when air resistance is absent. Formulated by Sir Isaac Newton in his Principia, it dictates planetary orbits around the Sun. For the point, name this attractive force between any two objects with mass.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is modernly described by general relativity as spacetime curvature and classically by Newton's inverse-square law.

quizzes.question: Known in Nepalese as Sagarmatha, this geographical feature forms part of the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region. Standard climbing routes up this mountain include the South Col from Nepal and the North Ridge from Tibet. Reaching an official elevation of over 29,000 feet, it was first successfully scaled in 1953 by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay. For the point, name this tallest peak in the world.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest features climbing routes like the South Col and North Ridge and is the world's tallest peak above sea level.

quizzes.question: For an object in uniform circular motion, this quantity is directed inward toward the center of curvature and is termed centripetal. Because it is a vector quantity, an object moving in a circle at constant speed still experiences this change due to continuous redirection. Denoted by units of distance divided by time squared, it is zero for objects moving at a constant velocity in a straight line. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity.
quizzes.explanation: Centripetal acceleration changes the direction of velocity in circular motion even if speed remains constant.

quizzes.question: Recommended for its modern name in 1865 by British Surveyor General Andrew Waugh, this peak lies in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates. In Tibet it is known as Chomolungma, while in Nepal it is called Sagarmatha, and mountaineers crossing above 8,000 meters enter its treacherous 'Death Zone.' For the point, name this highest mountain above sea level on Earth, first officially summitted in 1953 by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level at 8,848.86 meters. It is known as Sagarmatha in Nepal, Chomolungma in Tibet, and was named after Sir George Everest by Andrew Waugh.

quizzes.question: Calculated as velocity squared divided by radius in circular motion to describe centripetal behavior, this vector quantity is measured in standard SI units of meters per second squared. According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, this value is directly proportional to the net force applied to an object and inversely proportional to its mass. For the point, name this physical quantity defined as the rate of change of an object's velocity over time.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is the vector quantity measuring the rate of change of velocity with respect to time, expressed in m/s² and related to force by F = ma.

quizzes.question: Situated along the international border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, this geological feature reaches an officially recognized height of 8,848.86 meters. The Royal Geographical Society named this peak after British surveyor Sir George Everest in 1865. For the point, name this Himalayan peak that was famously climbed to its summit for the first time on May 29, 1953.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest lies on the border of Nepal and China/Tibet and was first summitted on May 29, 1953, by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay.

quizzes.question: Einstein's Equivalence Principle states that the effects of this force in a static frame are indistinguishable from a pseudo-force in a uniformly accelerating reference frame. Described classically by an inverse-square law involving a constant approximately equal to 6.674 times 10 to the power of negative 11, it is the weakest of the four fundamental interactions. For the point, name this universal attractive force acting between any two masses.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is described by Newton's law of universal gravitation and Einstein's General Relativity, acting as an attractive interaction between masses.

quizzes.question: Climbers attempting to reach this mountain's summit must endure extreme oxygen deprivation above 8,000 meters in a region designated as the 'Death Zone.' Native Nepalese refer to this mountain as Sagarmatha, meaning 'Forehead of the Sky,' while its English name honors a former Surveyor General of India. For the point, name this tallest mountain in the world.
quizzes.explanation: The region above 8,000 meters on Mount Everest is called the Death Zone due to low oxygen levels. Its Nepalese name is Sagarmatha.

quizzes.question: For objects moving in a circular path at constant speed, the centripetal form of this quantity points continuously toward the center of curvature. Near Earth's surface, free-falling objects in a vacuum experience a standard constant value of this quantity equal to approximately 9.81 meters per second squared. For the point, name this kinematic quantity that measures how quickly velocity changes.
quizzes.explanation: Standard free-fall acceleration near Earth's surface is approximately 9.81 m/s², representing the change in velocity per second.

quizzes.question: Formed by the ongoing tectonic collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates, this mountain's Tibetan name translates to 'Mother Goddess of the World.' Surveyed by Andrew Waugh, who proposed naming it after his predecessor, this mountain rises to over 29,000 feet above sea level in the Himalayas. For the point, name this legendary mountain that stands as the world's highest peak.
quizzes.explanation: In Tibet, Mount Everest is called Chomolungma ('Mother Goddess of the World'). It was formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates.

quizzes.question: Modern physics models this phenomenon not as a simple action-at-a-distance, but as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy in General Relativity. Sir Isaac Newton formulated a law for this interaction showing that it varies inversely with the square of the distance between two bodies. For the point, name this attractive force that holds planets in orbit around the Sun.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is modernly described by Einstein's General Relativity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.

quizzes.question: New Zealander Sir Edmund Hillary and Sherpa mountaineer Tenzing Norgay achieved world fame on May 29, 1953, by reaching the summit of this peak. Located in the Mahalangur Himal range, it is the highest of the Seven Summits. For the point, name this massive mountain situated on the border of Nepal and China.
quizzes.explanation: Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay made the first officially confirmed ascent of Mount Everest on May 29, 1953.

quizzes.question: In the fundamental physics equation net force equals mass times this quantity, it is represented by the symbol a and is inversely proportional to mass for a given force. Because it requires both a magnitude and a direction to describe changes in speed or orientation, it is classified as a vector quantity. For the point, name this physical concept that describes how fast an object speeds up or changes direction.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is the 'a' in Newton's second law equation F = ma, defined as the rate of change of velocity.

quizzes.question: This geographic feature's local name in Tibet translates to 'Mother Goddess of the World', while in Nepal it is known as Sagarmatha. It was formed by the ongoing tectonic collision between the Indian and Eurasian plates, and its region above 8,000 meters is famously known as the 'Death Zone' due to severe hypobaric hypoxia. For the point, name this highest mountain above sea level on Earth, first summitted by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is known as Chomolungma in Tibet and Sagarmatha in Nepal. It was formed by tectonic collision, features the Death Zone above 8,000 meters, and was first officially climbed by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953.

quizzes.question: For an object undergoing uniform circular motion, the centripetal form of this vector quantity points continuously toward the center of the path and is calculated as speed squared divided by radius. According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, it is directly proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass. Expressed in the SI unit of meters per second squared, for the point, name this rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity per unit time. Centripetal acceleration equals v²/r, Newton's second law relates it via F = ma, and its SI unit is m/s².

quizzes.question: This landmark was surveyed during the Great Trigonometrical Survey and officially named in 1865 by the Royal Geographical Society upon the recommendation of Andrew Waugh. Located along the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, it stands at an officially recognized elevation of 8,848.86 meters. For the point, name this Himalayan peak named after a British Surveyor General.
quizzes.explanation: Andrew Waugh recommended naming the peak Mount Everest in 1865 in honor of his predecessor Sir George Everest. It is located on the Nepal-Tibet border and rises to 8,848.86 meters.

quizzes.question: Einstein's Equivalence Principle states that local experiences of this interaction are indistinguishable from being in a uniformly accelerating reference frame. Described classically as an attractive interaction operating over infinite distances with a constant equal to roughly 6.674 times 10 to the negative 11th power SI units, it causes free-falling objects near Earth to accelerate at 9.81 meters per second squared. For the point, name this weakest of the fundamental forces that acts between any two masses.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is calculated via Newton's law using the universal gravitational constant G, satisfies Einstein's Equivalence Principle, and produces a standard acceleration of 9.81 m/s² on Earth.

quizzes.question: Extreme atmospheric conditions above 8,000 meters on this physical feature create the hyper-hazardous 'Death Zone' where human survival without supplemental oxygen is severely limited. It forms part of the Mahalangur Himal sub-range in the Himalayas and belongs to the Seven Summits as the tallest peak on Earth. For the point, name this mountain that was first successfully climbed on May 29, 1953.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is situated in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range, contains the Death Zone above 8,000 meters, is part of the Seven Summits, and was first climbed on May 29, 1953.

quizzes.question: Near the surface of Earth, the standard value for a specific type of this quantity caused by gravity is approximately 9.81 meters per second squared. It occurs whenever an object changes its speed, direction of motion, or both, as it is a vector quantity describing velocity changes over time. Expressed mathematically as net force divided by mass, for the point, name this physical concept.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is a vector quantity representing the change in velocity over time. Near Earth's surface, gravitational acceleration is approximately 9.81 m/s², and Newton's second law defines it as a = F/m.

quizzes.question: Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary achieved international fame in May 1953 after becoming the first mountaineers confirmed to reach the summit of this giant landform. It lies along the boundary between the Tibet Autonomous Region of China and Nepal, where it is locally called Sagarmatha. For the point, name this highest peak on Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Sir Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay made the first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest on May 29, 1953. In Nepal, the peak is called Sagarmatha.

quizzes.question: In modern physics, Einstein's General Theory of Relativity describes this phenomenon as the curvature of spacetime resulting from the presence of mass and energy. Classically calculated using the formula F equals G times m one m two over r squared, it is the dominant force at astronomical scales because it is strictly attractive and operates across infinite distances. For the point, name this fundamental force responsible for keeping planets in orbit around the Sun.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is modernly understood through General Relativity as spacetime curvature caused by mass and energy, and classically modeled by Newton's law of universal gravitation.

quizzes.question: Andrew Waugh recommended naming this geographical feature after his predecessor, Sir George Everest, despite the British surveyor's own reservations. Located in the Himalayan range, it reaches an elevation of over 29,000 feet, making it the highest of the Seven Summits. For the point, name this world-famous mountain.
quizzes.explanation: Sir George Everest was the namesake recommended by Andrew Waugh in 1865 for the mountain, which stands as the highest peak among the Seven Summits.

quizzes.question: The formula a equals v squared divided by r calculates the centripetal variety of this physical quantity for an object moving in a circular path. Measured in SI units of meters per second squared, it equals zero for any body traveling at constant speed in a straight line. For the point, name this vector quantity defined as the rate of change of velocity.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time. Its centripetal formula is a = v²/r, its unit is m/s², and it is zero when moving at constant velocity in a straight line.
